title: Ops Seamless Canary Script — Pocketkit (iter0)
content:
Purpose and audience:
This is a compact, seller-facing technical pocketkit to help SEs and SRE-facing sellers run a live demo / pilot canary conversation that highlights Redwood's graceful degradation and fallback routing economics. Primary audience: platform SEs, solutions engineers, and seller-engineer pairs during pilot handoffs. Status: working draft — comments welcome.

One-line value prop to lead with:

- "When capacity or latency constraints hit, Redwood keeps the user experience alive: fast fallbacks, predictable cost, and clear SLO tradeoffs — without you rewriting prompts or model code."

Suggested 6-slide micro-deck (each slide = 30–60s):

1) Hook: Real problem statement (30s)
- "We built an AI feature your users love. During peak or training runs latency spikes and costs explode. How do you stay on and keep UX intact?"
- Quick stat to drop: typical LLM app sees 4–10x per-token cost variance during bursts (source: internal trace sampling).

2) How Redwood protects UX (40s)
- Smart routing: route by latency, cost, region, tenant tier.
- Model variants: high-fidelity -> mid -> cost-optimized quantized fallback.
- Prefix/KV cache and short-circuiting for repeated prompts.
- Visual: mini-flow of request -> router -> model v1 / fallback v2 / cache hit. (Speaker note: point to latency bands: <150ms, 150–500ms, >500ms)

3) Canary script (demo play) (60s)
- Setup: Two models pinned for the pilot: rwd-llama-70b (primary), rwd-llama-7b-q4 (fallback). Canary traffic: 5–10% of production-like traffic.
- Actions: ramp generator script (link to PLAT-2384), watch console: per-request latency, tokens, model chosen, and cost estimate.
- Observable win: when we inject a GPU throttling event, routing should move canary traffic to fallback and keep median latency under 600ms.

4) What to show in the Console (45s)
- Per-route breakdown: token counts, median p95/p99 latencies, model selection time.
- Cost delta visualization: show per-1k tokens cost spike avoided by fallback over time.
- Traces: example of a traced request that fell back and returned quick result.

5) Seller script / objection snippets (90s combined)
- Objection: "We care about quality — won't a fallback be worse?"
  - Response: "Fallback is a graded option. We keep the primary model for high-value flows, but route short/low-risk calls to fast variants and use A/B rollback if quality drift detected. We instrument quality with prompt sets and automatic evals so you never lose visibility."
- Objection: "What if fallbacks change app behavior?"
  - Response: "We can pin model versions to routes, add post-processing filters, and route only synthetic/low-importance calls through fallbacks during canaries. Also, we support deterministic sampling for debugging returns."
- Objection: "How do we validate it in our security posture?"
  - Response: "Private deployments keep data on VPC; Dedicated allows reserved capacity for sensitive workloads. We provide audit logs for every model decision and can run the canary inside customer's VPC if needed."

6) Quick checklist for a 20-minute pilot canary (use during demo)
- Pre-demo: confirm two model variants are available and pinned to test routes (rwd-llama-70b, rwd-llama-7b-q4).
- Start: baseline trace run (50 requests), collect median p95/p99.
- Inject: synthetic throttle (instructions in PLAT-2384) or increase load generator to 4x baseline.
- Observe: routing switch in Console, tokens/cost chart, trace of a fallback request.
- Rollback: revert routing or pause generator; confirm metrics return to baseline.
- Post-mortem: capture sample responses and attach to Confluence notes.

Tactics & rapid tips for SEs (cheat-sheet style)
- Always show economics: open Console, filter to route, toggle model timeline and cost projection. Numbers matter more than architecture words.
- Keep the customer’s risk surface small: demonstrate fallback only on search/summary endpoints first.
- Use prompt flags: tag requests as low-quality-check to route automatically during canary.
- Bring an SRE buddy to handle infrastructure toggles — shows low friction and confidence.

Measuring success (pilot metrics to capture)
- Latency: median, p95, p99 for route before/during/after canary.
- Quality: pass rate on 10 curated prompt-eval set before/during/after.
- Cost: per-1k token effective spend and cost avoided compared to no-fallback baseline.
- Operational: time-to-detect (console alert) and time-to-recover (routing change or auto-fallback).

Common pitfalls and how to avoid them
- Pitfall: overloading with canary traffic (-> noisy results).
  - Fix: start small (5%), increase incrementally with steady-state checks.
- Pitfall: mixing high-risk user flows into fallback set.
  - Fix: categorize endpoints and only route low-risk endpoints initially.
- Pitfall: no eval coverage for fallback outputs.
  - Fix: create lightweight automated eval that runs on fallback responses and surfaces regressions.

Open tasks / TODOs (notes to self)
- Create a one-pager with sample CLI commands to toggle routing for non-technical sellers. (TODO: Priya)
- Add a short trimmed video clip showing Console before/during/after. (TODO: Marcus)
- Draft a customer-facing one-pager for procurement explaining reserved capacity implications during fallbacks. (TODO: Tom)

References and quick links
- Canary design notes (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PLAT/Canary+and+Fallback+Design+Notes
- JIRA: PLAT-2384 (traffic generator + router experiments)
- Runtime PR (example): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/712

Speaker notes (rapid-fire)
- When pressed for time: skip slides 2 and 4; go straight to demo checklist and the cost chart.
- If the buyer is technical: show token-level tracing and the model selection decision JSON from the trace.
- If the buyer is non-technical: emphasize continuity of UX and dollars saved; avoid deep kernel/quantization talk.

Feedback wanted
- Is this pocketkit lightweight enough to carry in a 15–20 minute pilot? Which items are too engineering-heavy?
- Any missing objection types you repeatedly encounter in field calls?

Notes: draft tone intentionally conversational. This is meant to be copied into a slim deck or printed as a single-page leave-behind.
